create.title: Exact paired-interior moving-cell trace reduction and strict residual-mask obstruction
create.statement_tex: Fix A>0, q=4N, K=sqrt(NM), M^(3/4)(log(2X))^A<V<=K, M<=N^(1/2), and for every odd d|N put c=q/d, H=c/2, n=H/2. Retain the literal complex boundary profile, zero extension, asymmetric cell, signed blocks, transitions, half-open choices, and endpoints. Positive-prefix and negative-suffix Abel summation put the moving atom in with a positive sign on both blocks and expose, but do not estimate, the positive right outer endpoint, negative left outer endpoint, and two profile-bulk remainders. Complete half-period inversion with every odd divisor returns the physical prefix/suffix trace. Direct geometric interval summation proves the separate v=0 and v=n Abel-trace pieces are each <<M^(-1/4)X^epsilon. The full-frequency endpoint face has polynomials j^2+j+1 and j(j-1): the latter has two roots modulo every prime power, while the former has no 2-adic root, one root modulo 3 and no lift modulo 9, and two simple roots precisely at p congruent 1 mod 3; hence the endpoint face is target-safe. After deleting it, kappa(ell)=floor(sqrt(Nell)+1/2) and r(ell)=kappa(ell)^2-Nell give exact positive and negative strict selectors, with boundary weights W_+(k)=w_U((k^2-k+1)/N)e(sqrt(k^2-k+1)-k) and W_-(k)=w_U((k^2+k)/N)e(sqrt(k^2+k)-k). Thus C_int,U(V)=sum_ell chi_4(ell)[eta_+(ell)W_+(kappa(ell))+eta_-(ell)W_-(kappa(ell))]+O(M^(-1/4)X^epsilon). The boundary arguments are not ell and the two profiles do not pair automatically. The trace vanishes unless V asymp K, but there its support can have size M; its absolute capacity is M^(1/4)X^epsilon. The scalar target is X^epsilon, equivalently raw M^(3/4)X^epsilon; raw square-root is sufficient but stronger. Endpoint roots, cardinality, ordinary chi_4 Abel summation, the named standard discrepancy and completion placements, and audited primary sources through 25 August 2026 do not prove this strict bound. In the favorable fixed-endpoint unit-BV model, the most favorable stated transformed exponent-pair line still needs M>=N^(390/703)>N^(1/2). These are route-scoped capacities and a cutoff-dated source no-match, not a lower bound or universal impossibility theorem. The strict trace, both outer terms, both profile-bulk remainders, and the full paired matrix remain open.

Prove the literal strict signed residual-mask theorem, while treating both Abel outer endpoints and both profile-bulk remainders as separate open seams before claiming the full paired interior matrix.

update.statement_tex: Duke--Friedlander--Iwaniec Lemma 6.1 exactly matches each individual theta multiplier K(-v^2,-s;4N/d), including arbitrary composite modulus divisible by four and gcd strata, but is pointwise. Round 158 audits the exact boundary-frozen strict selected trace through 25 August 2026. Mullner's incomplete quadratic estimate accepts arbitrary even composite modulus and endpoints but no root-indexed coefficient; even after an unavailable diagonal-BV grant it has raw capacity N^(1/2) and needs M>=N^(2/3). Vaaler and audited pointwise exponent pairs apply only after favorable fixed-endpoint, unit-BV, and residual-phase-BV grants. The transformed pair (195/796,235/398) then needs M>=N^(390/703)>N^(1/2); this is the most favorable threshold only among the stated audited favorable-model lines. The literal residual boundary phases remain k-dependent coefficients, not fixed Fourier shifts. Fixed-modulus root theorems keep outer coefficients independent of the selected root, while the project coefficient is F_(k-1)(k) or F_(-k)(k), with two moving strict selectors, quotient character chi_4, and modulus 4N. No audited moment, character, floor, limiting-distribution, or modulus-average spectral theorem matches every interface. This is a cutoff-dated direct-interface no-match, not a source impossibility theorem or exponent result.

Full-frequency inversion minus the separately safe zero and Nyquist trace pieces gives an exact physical prefix/suffix trace. Its endpoint face is target-safe by complete p-adic root tables. The strict survivor is exactly sum_ell chi_4(ell)[eta_+(ell)W_+(kappa(ell))+eta_-(ell)W_-(kappa(ell))] with different boundary-frozen profiles at (k^2-k+1)/N and (k^2+k)/N. Endpoint roots, support, ordinary one-variable BV, standard discrepancy, classical exponent-pair, and incomplete-quadratic placements do not prove that strict bound in M<=N^(1/2). correct_rejected.reason: Corrected scope: the generic pre-inversion mixed-variation control permitted V M^(-3/4)X^epsilon, but the exact Round 158 moving-cell trace has selected support min(M,V)X^epsilon and vanishes unless V asymp sqrt(NM). Its literal absolute capacity is M^(-3/4)min(M,V)X^epsilon, hence M^(1/4)X^epsilon on a nonzero top block. This is still above the scalar target and supplies no signed cancellation.

reject.reason: The endpoint polynomials govern only s=k-1 on the positive side and s=-k on the negative side. The exact strict selectors retain all other prefix and suffix residuals.
The character quotient is ell=(k^2-s)/N, while the literal profile arguments are (k^2-k+1)/N<ell and (k^2+k)/N>ell in strict terms.
The two boundary arguments and residual phases differ, and the literal coefficient is complex. No equality or conjugacy identity is present.
The positive and negative selectors occupy different residual ranges and are disjoint; their union supplies no termwise cancellation.
Although chi_4 changes sign, kappa, the residual, the strict selector, boundary profile, and phase all change, with no weight-preserving bijection.
L_str(V)<<min(M,V)X^epsilon is unsigned. On the nonzero top block it can be M and gives only M^(1/4)X^epsilon after the atom weight.
Localization proves the moving trace is zero away from V asymp sqrt(NM), but on that range V>>M and the full M-sized selected support may remain.
The frozen D=1 scalar target is O_epsilon(X^epsilon). The M^(-1/4) bounds for special rows and the endpoint face are stronger errors, not the target definition.
After removing the M^(-3/4) atom scale, the scalar target requires raw M^(3/4), while raw square-root M^(1/2) would be sufficient but stronger.
The exact sharp residual selector may enter and leave O(M) times, so its zero-extended variation can reproduce the absolute M^(1/4) weighted capacity.
One-variable continuous BV of w_U does not control variation of the root-indexed boundary coefficient after multiplication by the sharp nearest-square residual mask.
The named Erdos--Turan second-derivative placement reaches raw M^(3/4) only when M>=N^(2/3), outside M<=N^(1/2).
The (1/6,2/3) placement has the same M>=N^(2/3) threshold and is only an upper capacity for a favorable model.
Even after fixed-endpoint, unit-BV, and residual-phase-BV grants, the audited transformed pair needs M>=N^(390/703)>N^(1/2).
After an unavailable diagonal-BV grant, the raw completion capacity is sqrt(N)X^epsilon and requires M>=N^(2/3).
The strict selector has endpoints moving with kappa(ell), and its coefficient is root-indexed. Fixed-endpoint interval polynomials do not supply those missing variation estimates.
The phases e(sqrt(k^2-k+1)-k) and e(sqrt(k^2+k)-k) retain k-dependence and belong in the coefficient unless a separate BV or joint theorem controls them.
The trace pieces require their own prefix/suffix interval proof. Round 158 supplies that direct proof; whole-row theorems are not transferred.
The safe endpoint deletes only two boundary faces. The strict prefix and suffix selected sum remains open.
The dyadic family proves only an arithmetic selected point with nonresonant endpoint; actual profile nonvanishing and large aggregate signed mass are not proved.
The positive right endpoint and negative left endpoint are exact and quarantined, but no target estimate for either is proved.
Both profile-difference remainders and both outer endpoints lie outside the isolated moving-cell trace, so even a trace theorem would not close the paired matrix.
When c=4, H=2 and the zero and Nyquist frequencies exhaust the half-period; the paired interior set is empty.
The source conclusion is limited to audited primary theorems through 25 August 2026 and explicit interfaces; it does not rule out another or future coefficient-sensitive theorem.
The strict trace and additional paired-matrix seams remain open, as do many other M1 and all M2 owners, endpoint uniformity, M9, and the bridge.
